@graph.name: FUMD-AI Preprocessing Workflow
@graph.description: Turns raw SUMO (vehicle mobility) and OMNeT++ (cellular network) simulation output into a labeled, AI-ready dataset of cellular handover/migration events. Seven Jupyter notebooks, numbered 1-7 in run order, cover the pipeline: parse raw simulator output (1), add past-position lag columns (2), generate the OMNeT++ feature matrix (3), merge it with SUMO trajectories (4), fix placeholder past-position values (5), label migration/destination - the AI-ready dataset (6), and optional diagnostic visualizations (7). A master notebook, run_pipeline.ipynb, calls all seven in order via papermill from one set of top-level parameters, so the whole workflow can be run with a single notebook invocation instead of running each step by hand; the individual step notebooks also remain fully usable on their own. Every notebook's default parameters chain onto the tiny bundled example-data/ directory, so the whole workflow is runnable immediately after downloading, with no edits, against a small synthetic (non-real) dataset. See README.md for the full step-by-step description, inputs/outputs, and how to run each step (including headless/parameterized execution with papermill). Unless otherwise indicated, source code is MIT-licensed and explanatory text/figures are CC BY 4.0; input datasets retain the licences stated in their own metadata/source records.

@graph.name: Master pipeline: run the full workflow end-to-end
@graph.description: Orchestrator notebook that calls Steps 1-7 (notebooks/step_1_...ipynb through notebooks/step_7_...ipynb) in order via papermill, passing each step's output into the next from one set of top-level parameters. Writes every intermediate/final file, plus a fully executed copy of each step notebook for provenance, under OUTPUT_DIR. Run from the repository root, same as the individual step notebooks.

@graph.name: Step 1: Parse raw SUMO and OMNeT++ simulation output
@graph.description: Turns the two genuinely raw simulator outputs - a SUMO fcd-output XML file and an OMNeT++ .vec vector file - into the flat CSVs the rest of the workflow reads: parse_sumo_fcd() streams the XML into a per-vehicle-per-timestep trajectory CSV, and either extract_omnet_vectors() (external extractvectors tool) or extract_omnet_vectors_pure_python() (dependency-free, selected via OMNET_EXTRACTOR_METHOD) pulls the named network-quality vectors out of the .vec file into a long-format CSV.

@graph.name: Step 2: Add past-position columns
@graph.description: Adds lagged x-1..x-7/y-1..y-7 past-position columns to the Step 1 SUMO CSV (SUMO's own 999999 'no history yet' sentinel is left as-is here; Step 5 replaces it later, after Step 4's merge).

@graph.name: Step 3: Generate the OMNeT++ feature matrix
@graph.description: Cleans a raw OMNeT++ vector export and pivots it into a wide, per-vehicle-per-timestep table of network-quality metrics, with lagged/lead serving-cell columns.

@graph.name: Step 4: Merge SUMO trajectories with the OMNeT++ feature matrix
@graph.description: Aligns SUMO and OMNeT++ vehicle ids using a mapping file and merges the SUMO trajectory with the Step 3 network-metric matrix.

@graph.name: Step 5: Fix placeholder past-position values
@graph.description: Replaces the 999999 sentinel SUMO uses for 'no history yet' in the lagged position columns with each vehicle's first known coordinate.

@graph.name: Step 6: Label cell migrations (the AI-ready dataset)
@graph.description: Reconstructs each vehicle's stable serving-cell history and labels every row with migration (0/1/2, pre-handover warning window) and destination (the cell the vehicle will actually settle on). Produces the final AI-ready dataset. Imports src/fumd_workflow for the trajectory-reconstruction and migration-labeling logic.

@graph.name: Step 7 (optional): Visualize and sanity-check the migration labels
@graph.description: Supplementary/exploratory notebook: diagnostic plots (time spent in unstable mobility, event-type distribution, events per vehicle, spatial map of handovers) over the Step 6 outputs. Not required to produce the AI-ready dataset.

@graph.name: Trajectory reconstruction and migration-labeling logic
@graph.description: build_trajectories() and annotate_migrations(): shared, importable implementation of the stable-serving-cell trajectory reconstruction and handover/ping-pong event classification used by Step 6.

@graph.name: OMNeT++
@graph.description: Discrete-event network simulation framework used to generate the raw .vec vector output this workflow parses (Step 1) and cleans/pivots (Step 3).

@graph.name: Simu5G
@graph.description: OMNeT++ model of 4G/5G cellular networks used to simulate the serving-cell/SINR/CQI/RLC metrics this workflow labels handover events from.

@graph.name: INET Framework
@graph.description: OMNeT++ networking-protocol model library that Simu5G/Veins build on.

@graph.name: Veins
@graph.description: Vehicular network simulation framework coupling OMNeT++ with SUMO; produces the SUMO<->VEINS/OMNeT id mapping this workflow's Step 4 consumes.

@graph.name: SUMO
@graph.description: Microscopic vehicle-traffic simulator; its fcd-output XML is this workflow's Step 1 raw SUMO input.

@graph.name: netperfmeter (extractvectors)
@graph.description: Provides the extractvectors command-line tool Step 1's extract_omnet_vectors() shells out to, to pull named vectors out of a raw OMNeT++ .vec file. Built from source and validated against real OMNeT++ output; part of the INET 4.5.4 toolchain (see #inet). Optional: Step 1's OMNET_EXTRACTOR_METHOD='python' option reads the .vec file directly instead, with no external tool.

@graph.name: RAW_SUMO_XML_PATH
@graph.description: Raw SUMO fcd-output XML file (the simulator's own --fcd-output), one <timestep> element per simulated tick containing one <vehicle> element per vehicle present.

@graph.name: RAW_OMNET_VEC_PATH
@graph.description: Raw OMNeT++ .vec vector file (the simulator's own vector recording output): declaration lines mapping numeric vector ids to car/module/statistic names, followed by <id, event, time, value> data rows.

@graph.name: SUMO_OUTPUT_PATH
@graph.description: Base SUMO trajectory CSV parsed from the raw fcd-output XML: one row per vehicle per timestep, columns t, veh_id, x, y, angle, speed, pos, lane, slope, signals.

@graph.name: RAW_OMNET_PATH
@graph.description: Raw OMNeT++ vector export CSV (tab-separated Time/Object/Vector/Value). Step 3's own default points at the bundled example-data/raw_omnet_export.csv rather than chaining onto Step 1's OMNET_OUTPUT_PATH, so Step 3 onward is runnable without the external extractvectors tool Step 1 depends on.

@graph.name: OUTPUT_MATRIX_PATH / OMNET_PATH
@graph.description: Wide-format OMNeT++ feature matrix, one row per vehicle per resampled tick.

@graph.name: VEHICLES_PATH
@graph.description: SUMO trajectory CSV (Step 1 output plus Step 2's lagged x-1..x-7/y-1..y-7 past-position columns), one row per vehicle per timestep.

@graph.name: MAPPING_PATH
@graph.description: Vehicle id mapping between the SUMO and OMNeT++/VEINS simulations, produced by the simulation tooling itself (one 'SUMO=<id> VEINS=<id>' entry per line).

@graph.name: COMBINED_PATH
@graph.description: SUMO trajectory merged with the OMNeT++ feature matrix.

@graph.name: OUTPUT_PATH (Step 5)
@graph.description: Combined dataset with the 999999 placeholder sentinel replaced in the lagged position columns.

@graph.name: dataset_labeled_w<W>.csv
@graph.description: Final AI-ready dataset: input dataset plus migration and destination label columns.

@graph.name: NOTEBOOKS_DIR
@graph.description: Directory containing the step_1...step_7 notebooks that run_pipeline.ipynb calls via papermill.

@graph.name: OUTPUT_DIR
@graph.description: Directory run_pipeline.ipynb writes every intermediate/final pipeline output into, plus an executed/ subfolder holding a fully executed copy of each step notebook for provenance.

@graph.name: RUN_SUMO_PARSE
@graph.description: Whether run_pipeline.ipynb should actually invoke Step 1's parse_sumo_fcd(); defaults to True in the master notebook (a full pipeline run needs this), unlike Step 1's own standalone default of False.

@graph.name: RUN_OMNET_EXTRACT
@graph.description: Whether run_pipeline.ipynb should actually invoke Step 1's vector extraction (extract_omnet_vectors() or extract_omnet_vectors_pure_python(), per OMNET_EXTRACTOR_METHOD); defaults to False since the default extractor requires the external extractvectors tool. When True, Step 3 automatically reads Step 1's output instead of the RAW_OMNET_PATH parameter.

@graph.name: OMNET_EXTRACTOR_METHOD
@graph.description: Which of Step 1's two vector-extraction implementations RUN_OMNET_EXTRACT invokes: 'extractvectors' (default, shells out to the external netperfmeter tool) or 'python' (dependency-free, reads the .vec file directly; cross-checked against real extractvectors output - identical Time/Object/Value content, fewer rows since it excludes non-car modules and the redundant LTE-stack servingCell duplicate at the source, and full source-file float precision preserved - but slower on very large files since it is pure Python and single-threaded).

@graph.name: RUN_VISUALIZATION
@graph.description: Whether run_pipeline.ipynb should run the optional Step 7 diagnostics/plots notebook after Step 6.

@graph.name: WINDOW_S_VALUES
@graph.description: Pre-handover warning window(s), in seconds, that Step 6 labels (and Step 7 visualizes).

@graph.name: TOL_S
@graph.description: Step 6's stable-run tolerance: a run counts as stable if its duration is at least WINDOW_S - TOL_S.
